headline: South Africa's Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize
summary: The renowned human rights activist and former UN official has been awarded the prestigious prize for her lifelong commitment to justice.
details: South African human rights activist Navi Pillay has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize this year.
Pillay is widely recognized for her own lifelong dedication to fighting for human rights and justice across the globe.
She has previously served as the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights and has played a critical role in various international investigations.
The award recognizes her efforts in holding powerful entities accountable and her bravery in speaking truth to power.
In a lighthearted moment, Pillay joked that she could potentially share the prize with Donald Trump.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres has hailed the award as a a fitting recognition of her extraordinary contributions to peace and peace-building.
caption:
A lifelong champion of human rights and former UN official has just been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

South African human rights activist Navi Pillay has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize this year.

Pillay is widely recognized for her own lifelong dedication to fighting for human rights and justice across the globe.

She has previously served as the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights and has played a critical role in various international investigations.

The award recognizes her efforts in holding powerful entities accountable and her bravery in speaking truth to power.

In a lighthearted moment, Pillay joked that she could potentially share the prize with Donald Trump.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres has hailed the award as a a fitting recognition of her extraordinary contributions to peace and peace-building.

headline_marked: 700 auto-rickshaws: [[Leader backing drivers' demands owns 700 vehicles]], claims DNCC
headline: 700 auto-rickshaws: Leader backing drivers' demands owns 700 vehicles, claims DNCC
summary: DNCC Administrator Safiqul Islam Khan alleges a major political party's secretary general owns hundreds of auto-rickshaws while advocating for drivers.
details: Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) Administrator Safiqul Islam Khan claimed that a leader advocating for auto-rickshaw drivers' demands owns 700 auto-rickshaws himself.
The claim was made during an artwork programme on the pillars of the metro rail between Mirpur-12 and Agargaon on Friday morning.

Safiqul referred to the secretary general of a major political party, in an apparent reference to Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar, who had previously urged the government to accept drivers' demands.
The Administrator described the statement as 'ridiculous' and alleged that an investigation found the leader's ownership of the vehicles.
Safiqul also criticized political activists who participated in the auto-rickshaw movement, alleging that some parties are pushing sidewalk vendors into 'unethical activities'.
He recalled a recent clash in Mirpur on September 30, where illegal occupants were evicted from pavements, leading to violence and the burning of garbage trucks.
Safiqul warned that anyone attempting to re-occupy the footpaths would be thwarted, stating he is ready to stop any fresh conspiracy.
A monitoring team has been formed to ensure footpaths remain free of illegal occupation in every part of Dhaka city.
